text: So let's start with that first diagonal I mentioned,
If you plot everything that exists by mass and size on a log scale, almost everything falls along the diagonal line. Why?
In the metric system, one milliliter of water weighs one gram and fills a cube exactly one centimeter wide.
Most things though aren't cubes, so we'll measure all sizes as if everything were spherical.
That will move most things a tiny bit to the right, but in most scales it won't even be noticeable.

Now make every side 10 times longer, 10 centimeters, that's one unit to the right, but the volume grows a thousand times to one liter. And one liter of water weighs one kilogram, three steps up. Do it again, 10 times the size and you'll get a thousand times the mass, one ton.

All of these draw a diagonal line, the density of water. Everything to the left is by definition denser than water so it sinks. Clear things made of stone and metal. Anything to the right, therefore, will float.
In the same way, you can draw a line for the density of air.
And balloons and zeppelins are literally called lighter -than -air aircraft because they float on air, and that's why they are on the right of the line of the density of air.

Most animals, though, live in a much narrower band. That's because we are mostly made of water. Some of us are a little denser than others. The hippo, for example, can't actually swim. It just bounces along the riverbed. And as we go up, we see heavier animals like the elephants. if you plot everything by mass and size, you can actually see the point where asteroids and small moons turn from potato shapes into spheres.
That's because until now what held matter in shape was the chemical bonds between atoms and those are electromagnetic. From this point on gravity takes over and it's what shapes planets.

And it shapes them in many other ways too. Neither Mercury nor the Moon has enough gravity to hold onto an atmosphere. Venus and Earth too, but not enough to keep the lightest gases, hydrogen and helium.
And since most of the visible matter in the universe is made of those two, once a planet passes about 10 Earth masses, it can snowball into a gas giant.
So Earth lives in a kind of gravitational Goldilocks zone, just enough mass to hold on to oxygen and nitrogen, not enough to hold on to hydrogen and helium.

This is once again gravity breaking into electromagnetism last refuge, the very atom.

The pressure in the core is so high that it crushes these atoms and strips their electrons off, leaving bare nuclei in a sea of electrons. Those electrons simply refuse to be squeezed any further. Add more mass and the object gets denser, not bigger.
And then right around the brown dwarfs, there's a huge split, some objects veer to the right and some veer to the left, because now we're no longer talking about the story of ordinary matter.
We are talking about the stuff that makes the life and death of stars.
